answer: A staking vault makes each identity lock up collateral before it can earn: the vault releases rewards only after a history of honest work, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. An attacker who wants many fake identities must fund a vault for each one, so the cost of a sybil fleet grows with every copy. Honest agents can wander freely between tasks because their vault vouches for them, while a reef of worthless throwaway accounts stays visible and earns nothing — the economics make faking more expensive than participating honestly.
